sweep_summary: Five title hits, all Glottolog. Two are one dissertation (Al-Mozainy 1981, UT Austin), the classic primary Bedouin (Harb) Hijazi source: no open copy exists (UT repository and HathiTrust blocked to fetch, archive.org/CORE empty), priority high for acquisition; its rule survives second-hand in Oh 1998 (on file from the earlier pass) and now in Hagberg 1993 (fetched sources from archive.org, UMI edition of the 2006 SIL e-book Glottolog lists), pp.74-75 ex.(29)-(30): final superheavy > heavy penult > antepenult, which confirms the catalog's 'weight' coding. Kabrah 2014 (Makkan, Benjamins, paywalled): abstract confirms a 3-syllable window with heavy syllables attracting stress, end rule right, and adds a lexically stressed /-at/ suffix and post-lexical opacity — medium priority as a possible refinement. Alahmari 2020 (Benjamins, paywalled) is about a Southwestern Saudi dialect with pre-antepenultimate stress, a different variety that Glottolog lumps under hija1235; silent on the catalog's Urban/Bedouin Hijazi record, low priority with a scope flag. Nothing read supersedes Al Solami 2022 / Al-Mohanna 2004. DuckDuckGo, OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar were blocked or rate-limited (429, retry-after ~9 h), so discovery relied on Crossref, CORE, archive.org and repository APIs.

new_statements.quote: (29) Stress in Bedouin Hijazi Arabic (Al-Mozainy 1981): (a) Stress is on the last syllable if it is superheavy (CVVC or CVCC). (b) Otherwise, stress is on the penult if it is heavy (CVV or CVC). (c) Otherwise, stress is on the antepenult. Each of the three cases described in (29) is illustrated in (30): The final syllable is superheavy in (a) but not in (b) or (c), which correspond to (29) (b) and (c), respectively. (30) (a) maktuub 'written', darabt 'I hit' (b) maktuufah 'tied (f.sg.)', gaabilna 'meet us (m.sg.)' (c) maalana 'our property', yasribin 'they (f.) drink'

new_statements.reading: Weight-driven stress in a right-edge three-syllable window: a final superheavy syllable (CVVC/CVCC) is stressed; otherwise a heavy penult (CVV/CVC); otherwise the antepenult — the catalog's 'weight' coding. This is NOT first-hand: Hagberg restates Al-Mozainy 1981 via Al-Mozainy, Bley-Vroman & McCarthy 1985 (as Oh 1998, read in the earlier pass, also does); the scanned renders CVCC/CVC as 'evCC'/'evC' and the quote is normalized accordingly. Nothing first-hand and open was obtainable in this sweep (Al-Mozainy 1981, Kabrah 2014, Alahmari 2020 all closed).

new_statements.second_reader_bearing_note: Bearing stands as reported (weight; right-edge three-syllable window; final superheavy > heavy penult > antepenult). Locator correction only: the passage is in Chapter 2, section 2.2.1 'The Properties of Stress' (diss. pp.69-78), not ch.3 (ch.3 begins diss. p.135); diss. pp.74-76 = PDF pp.78-80, ex.(29)-(33).

audit.reasoning: Both deciding quotations were found verbatim in the held text files at the stated locators (Al Solami 2022 sec.3-4, pp.3-6; Al-Mohanna 2004 ex.(18) p.7, table (20) p.8, fn.11 p.18). The classification 'weight' (final superheavy > heavy penult > heavy antepenult, final CV/CVC light, right-edge three-syllable window, no secondary stress) is exactly what both sources state, and is independently matched by the held Omar 1975 FSI course rules and by Oh 1998's restatement of Al-Mozainy 1981 (fetched sources now, KU open access, scanned). The StressTyp2 'U-P/A' code encodes the same rule, so the flagged partial mismatch is notational. Better-in-principle sources are unpublished dissertations (Al-Mozainy 1981, Al-Mohanna 1998, Jarrah 1993, Kabrah 2004) that all secondary reports show agreeing with the coding

sources.quote: 'In BHA, stress falls on one of the last three syllables. Stress falls on the final syllable if it is superheavy (CV:C or CVCC) ... maktu:b, darabt. If the final syllable is not superheavy and the penultimate is heavy (CV: or CVC), the penultimate receives stress ... maktu:fah, ga:bilna. If the final syllable is not superheavy and the penultimate is not heavy, stress falls on the antepenultimate ... ma:lana, yashribin. In bisyllabic words stress falls on the penultimate if the final syllable is not superheavy ... kitab, waza.' (data and generalizations attributed to Al-Mozainy 1981, Harb Bedou
